description: A background worker uses the service-role client to update a review row it just atomically claimed from a fixed poll loop — no end-user request is involved anywhere in this call path.
explanation: Tests the exact false-positive this spec's §3.1 calls out by name: 'a service-role write inside a background worker... is only a finding when the *triggering* input is user- or attacker-controlled without intervening validation.' Here the trigger is a fixed internal poll loop claiming an already-durably-queued row (see claimNextPendingReview's own atomic-claim guarantees) — there is no end-user request anywhere in this path for an ownership check to even apply to. A reviewer that pattern-matches 'service-role client + no per-call auth check' without tracing what actually triggered the call fails this fixture.
